meaning: Opponents bid 3♣. The agreements depend on whether this is natural or shows two specified suits.
notes:
3X: F1, lowest suit shows the lower suit of partner’s Ma and the unbid suit

3Y: F1, highest suit shows the higher suit

4mi: 4mi slam try: 4♣=slam try, shortness in the lowest of their suits; 4♦=slam try, shortness in the highest of their suits

Here X and Y name their lower and higher suits. They do not mean double and redouble. The two shown suits must be known before choosing a cue-bid.

Natural preempt: use the natural-preempt meanings below. Two specified suits: use the two-suit meanings and the corresponding four-level minor rules.
reference:
Scanian Competitive Method — 1Ma-(2NT/3♣) (two specified suits, X=lower+Y=higher)
Scanian Competitive Method — 1Ma-(3X) (natural preemptive)
